description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the s473t6c review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/t6c/p1923-kvslice.pl row D; the same on main c7f89fa8 and on the t6c tree, so PRE-EXISTING and the sibling #1923 did not reach (CLAUDE.md rule 11: count the parse paths).

  my %h = (a => 1, b => 2, c => 3);
  my $d1 = delete %h{"a"};      # perl 1 (the list (a, 1) in scalar context = its last element)   PCL 2
  my @d2 = delete %h{"b"};      # b 2 on both (list context is right)

#1923 (s473t6c) routed gen_kv_hash_slice_form and gen_kv_array_slice_form through `_slice_in_context_form`; the `delete` of a kv-slice is emitted elsewhere (grep Pl/ExprToCL.pm for the delete arm that accepts a kv-slice operand) and still returns the raw list whose scalar coercion is a count.  Probe `delete @h{...}` in scalar context too (perl: the last deleted VALUE) -- if that one is right, its wrapper is the one to reuse.

BAR: emission change -> corpus-diff (expect ~no corpus sites), gen bump, guard rows in Pl/t/kvaslice-01.t beside #1923's.  Low frequency.

=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED 1e331b02.  #1923 routed the kv-slice READ emitters through
`_slice_in_context_form`; the `delete` arm of gen_funcall_form builds its own
form and was left behind, so `my $d = delete %h{"a"}` answered the pair COUNT
(2) where perl answers the VALUE (1).

WIDER THAN FILED, and the probe is why: all FOUR slice kinds were wrong, not
only the kv pair the task named -- `delete @h{"c","d"}` and `delete @arr[2,3]`
in scalar context answered their counts too.  And it is not merely a wrong
number: a count is always TRUE, so `delete %j{"q"}` on a ZERO value read as
true.  The two ELEMENT kinds return one value and are deliberately NOT wrapped.

Ten shapes probed vs perl 5.40.3, identical after
(scratch/s492a/probes/m7-delete.{pl,perl.out,tree.out}).  docs/ir-spec.md 3.2e
says it normatively.  Guard: 3 rows in Pl/t/kvaslice-01.t (18 -> 21) beside
#1923's; rows 19-20 FAIL on a 268d7e00 extraction and the LIST-context /
element row passes (scratch/s492a/inverse-guards-base268.log).
subject: #1923 residue: `delete %h{...}` / `delete %a[...]` (a kv-slice DELETE) in SCALAR context answers the pair COUNT (2) where perl answers the LAST value -- the one kv-slice spelling that does not go through `_slice_in_context_form`
